profiles.speaker: TED
profiles.accent: weathered British coastal accent, rough and rural
profiles.timbre: gravelly, low and dry, with a smoker's rasp and a wheezy edge
profiles.voice_description: Gravelly older male, coastal accent. A weathered lighthouse keeper in his sixties or seventies with a low chest voice, deep rasp and a dry wheeze. Slow, clipped delivery that barks orders, grumbles under his breath and clears his throat or coughs mid-sentence. Sarcastic and impatient, with a faint buried warmth. Close and rough, projected to be heard over wind and stairwells.
profiles.preview_text: Eclipse, storm season, and the Saltgate howling. Of course they send a new money toff. Boiler's cold and the beacon's starving. Down to the engine room. Shovel coal, Isaac. Gauge is waking up. Put your back into it. Cracked clean through. The burner's finished. Hrmph. Nothing to mend up here.
canon_basis: chr_ted voice casting note: 'gravelly older male, coastal accent'
Character brief: gruff, snarky, old-school; grunts and coughs; calls city folk 'new money toffs'
Ted introduces the setting and each objective
profiles.contrast_note: Ted is the lowest, slowest and roughest voice, with a gravel rasp and coughs. Arthur is higher, thinner and faster, and Daniel is the brightest and youngest. Ted's flat low delivery is the easiest to tell apart in a storm.

profiles.speaker: ARTHUR
profiles.accent: lilting northern British sailor's accent, lighter than Ted's
profiles.timbre: wiry, reedy and thin with a slight crack, mid-high pitch
profiles.voice_description: Wiry, old, frantic male voice. An elderly sailor with a thin, reedy, slightly cracked mid-high voice and a light northern sea-faring lilt. Fast and clipped, wry and friendly at rest, with a rising, breathless, rattled edge under pressure. He shouts over an engine, stays wary and keeps a warm joking undertone. Clearly higher and more nasal than a gravelly bass.
profiles.preview_text: Easy now, we mean no harm. Just cold and wet. The gate, please? Ted, you old rock. Thought you'd be drowned by now. Keep her off the rocks, Isaac. Watch the water, not the dark. Too close! Give the rocks some room, Isaac. There! Ship's lights, out in the swell. She can't see the rocks. No beacon.
canon_basis: chr_arthur voice casting note: 'wiry, old, frantic'
Character brief: older sailor, wry and frantic under pressure, friendly but wary
profiles.contrast_note: Arthur is thin, reedy, fast and rising in pitch, where Ted is low, slow and gravelly. Compared with Daniel he is older, more cracked and wry, and his panic is controlled and urgent rather than nervous and chattering.

profiles.speaker: DANIEL
profiles.timbre: bright, smooth and light, slightly high-pitched, with a nervous tremble
profiles.voice_description: Young, enthusiastic male. A man in his early twenties with a bright, smooth, light tenor and a clean youthful southern English accent. Chatty and eager, with forced cheer that wobbles into anxiety. He trails off mid-sentence, laughs nervously, loses his breath and drops to a hushed half-whisper when spooked. No rasp or grit, warm and boyish.
profiles.preview_text: Down here suits me fine. Did the walls just... never mind. Warm is good. Arthur says it's just weather. I'm sure Arthur's right. He's usually right. Mostly. Did you hear that? Tell me you heard that. Pipes, right? Say pipes. Don't listen to it. Wind makes all sorts of voices. Hum something. I'm humming.
canon_basis: chr_daniel voice casting note: 'young, enthusiastic male'
Character brief: younger sailor, light-hearted and anxious
Shelters in the basement and stays there
profiles.contrast_note: Daniel is the youngest, brightest and smoothest voice, with no rasp, and his anxiety shows as trailing, tremulous chatter and nervous laughs. Ted is a low gravelly bark and Arthur is an older, thinner, cracked rasp. Daniel's lines are heard only in the basement, which also separates him.

lines.tts_text: [grumbling] Eclipse, storm season, and the Saltgate howling. Of course they send a new money toff. [coughs]
Boiler's cold and the beacon's starving. Down to the engine room. Shovel coal, Isaac.
[shouts] That's the firebox. Feed it coal, mind your sleeves, and don't stand gawping.
[grumbling] There she goes. Keep shovelling; the needle won't climb on good intentions.
[shouts] Gauge is waking up. Put your back into it.
Hear that dynamo whine? Good. Now up to the lantern room and look over the arc lamp.
[shouts] Arc lamp's in the middle. Open her up and look at the burner.
Cracked clean through. The burner's finished. [coughs] Hrmph. Nothing to mend up here.
Standing there won't warm the boiler. Think where the heat comes from, Isaac.
Basement, Isaac. The engine room. Coal's piled by the firebox.
[sighs] Go down to the engine room. Take the shovel. Load coal into the firebox.
[grumbling] Rowboat's moored at my dock. Stranded sailors, by the look. Go let them in at the island gate.
[grunts] See them? Soaked and stranded. The gate's down the path from the dock. Go on.
Easy now, we mean no harm. Just cold and wet. The gate, please?
[breathless] Good hands on that gate. Daniel, move. Quick, now.
Ted, you old rock. Thought you'd be drowned by now.
Thought the same of you. [coughs] Hrmph. Dry yourselves. The boy can warm up downstairs.
Down here suits me fine. Did the walls just... never mind. [nervous laugh] Warm is good.
Arthur says it's just weather. I'm sure Arthur's right. He's usually right. Mostly. [nervous laugh]
[breathless] Did you hear that? Tell me you heard that. Pipes, right? Say pipes.
[whispers] Don't listen to it. Wind makes all sorts of voices. Hum something. I'm humming. [nervous laugh]
Those sailors won't dry themselves on my dock, Isaac.
The gate, Isaac. Down the path from the dock. Someone's shouting out there.
Walk to the island gate and open it. Let them in.
[coughs] No burner, no beacon. Outpost, across the Gullwater. Go with Arthur, Isaac.
In you get. One hand on the wheel, eyes on the rocks.
[shouts] Keep her off the rocks, Isaac. Watch the water, not the dark.
[breathless] Too close! Give the rocks some room, Isaac.
[shouts] Hold on! Swing wide of the rock and steer clear. Gently now.
[hushed] There! Ship's lights, out in the swell. She can't see the rocks. No beacon.
There's the landing. Fetch the burner. I'll keep the engine turning.
[muttering] Nothing there for us. Leave it be. The burner, the burner.
[exhales] That's it? Good. Hold it close. Back across we go.
Ted wants that burner, Isaac. Boat's waiting on you.
[shouts] Come on! The outpost, across the Gullwater. Get in the boat.
Board the boat, take the wheel, steer for the outpost landing. Go!
Burner won't walk to the boat, Isaac.
[shouts] Find the burner! Keep looking. Look sharp!
Find the burner, pick it up, and bring it to the boat.

suggestions: Audition each preview_text in Voice Design and pick the closest of the generated previews before locking voice IDs. Check that the three voices stay distinct with storm and engine noise mixed in.

Ted's coughs and wheezes are tagged only where the delivery note asks for them. Consider recording the coughs and grunts as separate non-verbal one-shots to layer in, so the voice generation stays clean.
Arthur's lines shouted over the engine may need the engine bed mixed lower in the boat sections so his lines stay intelligible.
Daniel is only heard in the basement. Consider room reverb and a muffled, pipe-and-stone treatment in the mix rather than in the voice design.

The nudge ladders (I1, I2, I3 and O1, O2, O3) are set to rise in stability: I1/O1 are dry and varied, I2/O2 are louder, and I3/O3 are flat and clear. Check that the explicit tier is easy to understand in testing.
Tags are kept to at most two per line and placed only where the delivery note calls for them. If the model over-performs a tag, remove it and rely on the stability setting.
open_creator_decisions: Which lines are voiced and which are subtitle-only is a cost decision for the creator. This plan prepares all 39 lines.
Why Arthur and Daniel were on the water (smugglers?) is left open and nothing in the casting implies an answer.
Ted and Arthur's relationship is TBD in the lore. The 'drowned by now' exchange (ARTHUR_S2_05 and TED_S2_04) is a proposal, and its warmth is a delivery choice the creator may change.
Final accents (coastal, northern, southern) are casting suggestions built on the canon notes and can be shifted by the creator.
Fail-reason and outcome lines belong to the Story / Fail-State agent and are not cast here.
